query: Prior calculations on concentrated alloys examined variations in atomic mass and force constants, temperature-dependent lattice heat transport, or DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates; some estimates require a Debye temperature. The cited simulations generally represented perfect, defect-free bulk crystals. Experiments below 200 K indicate that lattice and electronic contributions in HfNbTaTiZr can be comparable, while measurements from 300 to 1200 K on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen report total conductivity of 10–17 W/(K m). Available analytical approaches do not capture all relevant atomic-scale complexity in refractory high-entropy alloys, and separate transport studies do not establish a predictive solution for this alloy. Given these constraints, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified new predictive approach make for HfNbTaTiZr without conflating lattice and electronic heat transport? Explain why it should outperform earlier approaches, quantify the expected improvement, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting observations from the cited work, and specify decisive comparisons with low- and high-temperature measurements that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: A spectral decomposition predictive approach that independently computes lattice and electronic thermal transport via detailed vibrational density of states (VDOS) and frequency‐resolved electron relaxation times from DFT, integrating MD-based Green–Kubo calculations with Boltzmann transport analysis.
generation.material_initial_state: Defect‐free, single‐phase HfNbTaTiZr alloy with meticulously controlled oxygen below 0.12 wt% to minimize extrinsic scattering.
generation.intervention: Implement a full-spectrum simulation protocol that (i) performs MD simulations to extract a high-resolution VDOS through Green–Kubo formalism for lattice transport and (ii) uses ab initio DFT calculations with frequency-resolved Boltzmann analysis to obtain electron relaxation times and plasma frequency shifts.
generation.conditions: Applicable for temperatures from ~100 K to 1200 K on samples produced with low oxygen and defect levels; below 100 K phonon quantization effects are acknowledged as a challenge.
generation.structural_mediator: The complete VDOS and detailed electron band dispersion, capturing force constant fluctuations and chemical disorder from first-principles calculations.
generation.mechanism: By decoupling the thermal transport channels, phonon contributions are computed using MD simulations with machine-learned force fields that capture scattering induced by force-constant disorder, while electronic contributions are separately determined using DFT-based Boltzmann transport with explicit evaluation of plasma frequency corrections and relaxation times. The two computed channels are then summed to yield the total thermal conductivity.
generation.predicted_outcome: The method is expected to predict total thermal conductivity within ±20% of experimental values over the 100–1200 K range, thereby outperforming earlier conflated Debye-based or linear-combination models by eliminating cross-contaminated estimates between lattice and electronic channels.
generation.baseline: Earlier models that rely on Debye temperature approximations and simplistic linear combination rules that conflate both contributions.
generation.boundary: The approach is primarily valid on high-purity, well-controlled samples and may require additional adjustments at very low temperatures (<100 K) where phonon quantization effects are pronounced.
generation.uncertainty: Uncertainty remains for low-frequency regimes where VDOS resolution may be challenging; however, the integration strategy is expected to control errors within the ±20% target. Any deviation beyond ±30% in channel decoupling would falsify the approach.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize high-purity HfNbTaTiZr samples and measure the VDOS using inelastic neutron scattering while obtaining electronic relaxation data via terahertz spectroscopy. Compare the separately computed lattice and electronic contributions with these measurements over the target temperature range.

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the independently computed lattice or electronic conductivity deviates by more than ±30% from the experimental measurements across the designated temperature range, then the hypothesis is falsified.

(3) Method 3: This scheme considers both the plasma frequency due to random changes in coordinating elements and the impact of lattice random distortions on relaxation time. For instance, the plasma frequency is calculated from a solid-solution model of HEAs using first principles, while the relaxation time is extracted from measurements using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS), which is an advanced technique for detecting changes in the electric-field amplitude and phase as it passes through a sample, allowing for the calculation of material dielectric properties and complex conductivity characteristics. Both values are then used in the Drude model to calculate low-frequency conductivity. The detailed calculation method is given in Supplementary Note 1, and the measurement of the relaxation time is included in Supplementary Note 3 and Supplementary Figs. 4, 5.

candidates.hypothesis: A machine learning (ML) based predictive model that decouples lattice and electronic heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr by training on a diverse dataset enriched with descriptors of short-range order (SRO), local lattice distortions, and electronegativity fluctuations.
candidates.intervention: Develop and deploy an ML model that leverages a comprehensive set of descriptors—including quantifiable SRO metrics (e.g., Warren–Cowley parameters from ab initio simulations), local lattice distortion measures (from DFT or advanced microscopy), and element-specific electronegativity differences—to independently predict the phonon and electron contributions to thermal conductivity.
candidates.changes: Enhanced clarity regarding the breadth and quality of training data, and explicitly acknowledged the current limitations regarding oxygen content. The descriptor set now includes validated experimental metrics of SRO, local lattice distortions, and electronegativity differences, ensuring that the ML model accurately decouples contributions.

minor_issues: Model accuracy may be limited if the training dataset is not sufficiently large or representative of real-world variations in oxygen content and microstructures.
Constraining oxygen below 0.2 wt% could make it difficult to directly compare to existing data on samples with higher oxygen levels.
fixes: Clarify how training or retraining will be conducted to handle different impurity levels, especially oxygen contents above 0.2 wt%.
Include a plan for data quality control and augmentation to ensure the ML model remains robust across a range of compositions and microstructures.
evidence_needs: Extensive published or newly measured data sets on HfNbTaTiZr with varied oxygen levels to confirm the generalizability of the ML approach.
Prior studies demonstrating successful incorporation of short-range order and local distortion descriptors into ML models for thermal transport predictions.

minor_issues: Reliance on supercell-based force-constant parameters requires careful validation for a multi-component alloy, given complex chemical disorder.

fixes: Demonstrate that the supercell calculations adequately capture force-constant fluctuations in five-component alloys.
Incorporate or reference empirical or ab initio validations of the chosen Drude-Lorentz parameters to handle compositional disorder.
evidence_needs: Comparison of the refined model’s lattice and electronic contributions to direct phonon and electron transport measurements at various temperatures.
Further data or literature verifying that supercell approaches remain accurate as the number of principal elements increases.
